page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized instance configuration designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications. The virtual machine delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores operating at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. Powered by Intel Xeon 8581C processors built on the x86_64 architecture, the server includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 372 GB, providing an elevated memory allocation of 7.75 GB per vCPU. The hardware integrates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets, enabling accelerated matrix arithmetic and vectorized operations directly on the CPU.

Benchmark evaluations position the c4-highmem-48 in the upper tier for integer manipulation, compilation, and cryptographic throughput. Geekbench scoring indicates strong processing capability, with software compilation tests reaching 41626 points and image processing benchmarks scoring in the top ten percent at 18689 points. The architecture also records notable throughput in web serving at 73.99 GB/s and robust bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 284.57 GB/s. For machine learning, the CPU executes prompt processing on smaller models at 2496.82 tokens per second using AMX. However, text generation performance on larger 70B parameter models drops to 2.74 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Additionally, the instance contains no local NVMe storage and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring cloud administrators to provision network storage volumes and external IP routing separately.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio minimizes the necessity of over-provisioning compute cores solely to satisfy memory footprint demands. The platform is best fitted for in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput database operations, enterprise ETL pipelines, continuous integration build servers, and static web serving workloads requiring significant memory headroom.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized cloud server engineered for resource-heavy workloads requiring extensive memory capacity relative to compute cores. Powered by the Intel Xeon 8581C processor running on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading, alongside 372 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX for accelerated matrix and vector calculations. Benchmark metrics demonstrate solid performance in software compilation, cryptography, image processing, and prompt processing for compact language models. The instance lacks bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached persistent storage for stateful data retention, and does not include dedicated GPU accelerators. Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-48 is well suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, analytical data processing, software build farms, and high-concurrency static web serving.
